item.title: Kerry TD says Taoiseach should call out attacks on Iran as breach of international law
item.description: Kerry Sinn Féin TD Pa Daly says the Taoiseach should call out the attacks on Iran as a breach of international law. Micheál Martin has blamed the war on failures of international institutions such as the United Nations, but has not condemned attacks by any side. Deputy Daly says it’s important for Ireland to use its voice on the international stage. item.title: Man accused of murdering Kenmare man Mike Gaine remanded in custody for another two weeks
item.description: The American man accused of murdering Kenmare farmer Mike Gaine has been remanded in custody for another two weeks. 54-year-old Michael Kelley, who had been residing in Tralee, appeared in Tralee District Court this morning. He’s accused of murdering Mike Gaine last March. Advertisement Michael Kelley faces one charge; that between the 20th and 21st March 2025, he murdered Mike Gaine at Carrig, Kenmare, contrary to common law. item.title: Ward Proud Of Irish Performance
item.description: The Republic of Ireland will regroup following defeat to France in their opening World Cup qualifier last night. Carla Ward’s side were beaten 2-1 at Tallaght Stadium, despite taking the lead through captain Katie McCabe in the first half. Advertisement Ireland now travel to Utrecht on Saturday to face the Netherlands, who drew 2-2 away to Poland. Elsewhere, Northern Ireland opened their campaign with a 2-0 defeat away to Switzerland.

item.title: O'Connor Best Prepared AFL Player Following Irish Off Season
item.description: Geelong coach Chris Scott says Kerry’s Mark O’Connor could be the best prepared player in Australian Rules. Scott praised O’Connor’s conditioning following his Club All-Ireland winning run with Dingle. O’Connor is entering his tenth season with the Geelong Cats and is just three games away from reaching 150 AFL appearances. item.title: Edogbo Follows Brothers Footsteps With Munster Senior Contract
item.description: Munster Rugby have confirmed that back-row forward Seán Edogbo will be promoted to the senior squad next season on a two-year contract. The 21-year-old from Cobh made his Munster debut against Dragons in January and was named Player of the Match. He previously represented Ireland at under-20 level and follows his brother Edwin in becoming a Munster senior player. Advertisement

item.title: Age Friendly Ireland Tralee event hears of need to address ageist workplace stereotypes
item.description: An event in Tralee organised by Age Friendly Ireland has heard that workplaces must adapt to reflect an increasingly age-diverse workforce. The organisation held its third Ambassadors’ Day in The Rose Hotel, to promote age and diversity at work. item.title: Man jailed for two and a half years for spate of burglaries in Tralee last year
item.description: A man has been jailed for two and a half years for carrying out a spate of burglaries in Tralee last August. 44-year-old Michael Coffey, previously of 32 Cnoc Gorm Tralee, was sentenced at Tralee Circuit Court by Judge Ronan Munro this afternoon. The judge suspended a portion of Mr Coffey’s sentence, telling him the safest thing for the people of Kerry would be for him to get a job. item.title: Farrell Names Team For Friday Night Clash With Wales
item.description: Ireland Name Team For Six Nations Clash With Wales Ireland head coach Andy Farrell has named his side for Friday night’s Guinness Men’s Six Nations clash with Wales at the Aviva Stadium, with kick-off at 8.10pm. Jamison Gibson-Park will reach a major milestone as he earns his 50th Ireland cap, while Ulster scrum-half Nathan Doak could make his international debut from the bench.
